'''George William Series''' {{post-nominals|list=[[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]]}} (22 February 1920 – 2 January 1995) was a British [[physicist]], notable for his work on the optical [[spectroscopy]] of [[hydrogen]] [[atom]]s.

== Early life and education ==
Series was born in [[Bushey|Bushey Heath]], [[Hertfordshire]], the son of William Series (1892–1959) and his wife Alice (1889–1976), {{nee|Crosthwaite}}.<ref name=":0">{{Cite ODNB|last1=Stacey|first1=Derek|id=57757|title=Series, George William}}</ref>  Aged ten he won a scholarship to [[Queen Mary's Grammar School, Basingstoke|Queen Mary's Grammar School]], [[Basingstoke]], and later to [[Reading School]].  In 1938 he was awarded an open scholarship and matriculated at [[St John's College, Oxford|St John's College]], [[Oxford]], where he graduated with first class honours in 1947,<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whowaswho/U175376|title=Who's Who|website=www.ukwhoswho.com|access-date=2016-06-03}}</ref> his studies having been interrupted by the [[World War II|Second World War]] (during the war Series, a [[conscientious objector]], served with the [[Friends' Ambulance Unit]] in [[Egypt]], [[Italy]], and Yugoslavia).  He took his MA and DPhil from Oxford in 1950.<ref name=":0" /> His PhD thesis is titled ''Applications of high resolution spectroscopy to problems of atomic structure'' and his supervisor was [[Heinrich Gerhard Kuhn]].<ref>{{cite Q|Q58858540}}</ref>

== Career ==
Series became a university [[lecturer]] in 1951 and a fellow of [[St Edmund Hall, Oxford|St Edmund Hall]] in 1954.  During this time he studied the structure of the hydrogen atom, becoming 'a world authority on the subject'.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/obituaryprofessor-george-series-1567497.html|title=Obituary:Professor George Series|date=1995-01-11|website=The Independent|language=en-GB|access-date=2016-06-03}}</ref>  In the 1950s and 1960s he exploited techniques developed by [[Alfred Kastler]]'s research group in Paris and  demonstrated that [[radiation]] from a coherent superposition of excited states of atoms would display interference effects, known as '[[quantum beats]]'.<ref name=DoddMemories>{{cite journal|journal=Physica Scripta|volume=T70|pages=5|first= J N|last=Dodd|date=1997|title=Editorial|doi=10.1088/0031-8949/1997/T70/E02|doi-access=free}}</ref>  A group of important papers on this subject brought Series international recognition.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=GWSmemorial>{{cite journal|journal=Physica Scripta|pages=3–172|title=George W Series Memorial Essays|date=1997|volume=T70|doi=10.1088/0031-8949/1997/t70/e01|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=qb2>{{cite journal|journal=Proceedings of the Physical Society|date=1959|pages=789–791|volume=74|first1=J N|last1=Dodd|first3=G W|last3=Series|first2=W N|last2=Fox|first4=M J|last4=Taylor|title=Light Beats as Indicators of Structure in Atomic Energy Levels|issue=6|bibcode=1959PPS....74..789D|doi=10.1088/0370-1328/74/6/122}}</ref><ref name=qb1>{{cite journal|journal=Proceedings of the Royal Society of London. Series A, Mathematical and Physical Sciences|date=1961|pages=1314|volume=263|first1=J N|last1=Dodd|first2=G W|last2=Series|title=Theory of Modulation of Light in a Double Resonance Experiment}}</ref>

He accepted a chair at [[University of Reading|Reading University]] in 1968, which he held until his retirement in 1982.<ref name=":0" />  In 1972 Series was the William Evans Visiting Professor at the [[University of Otago]]; in 1982 the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] awarded him a Raman Visiting Professorship and he was made an Honorary Fellow in 1984.<ref name=":2"/>

Series was elected a fellow of the [[Royal Society]] in 1971, and of the [[Royal Astronomical Society]] in 1972.  In 1982 he received the William F. Meggers award and the medal of the [[The Optical Society|Optical Society of America]].<ref name=":1" />

Series died in Oxford in 1995.

== Family ==
Series met his wife Annette (daughter of John Edward Pepper, a [[Civil service|civil servant]]) at Oxford; she read modern languages at [[St Hilda's College, Oxford|St Hilda's College]], and they were married on 21 December 1948.  They had four children: three sons Robert, John, and Hugh, and a daughter [[Caroline Series|Caroline]], who is a notable [[mathematician]] and fellow of the Royal Society.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://homepages.warwick.ac.uk/~masbb/|title=Caroline Series's homepage|website=homepages.warwick.ac.uk|access-date=2016-06-03|archive-date=13 March 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120313100010/http://homepages.warwick.ac.uk/~masbb/|url-status=dead}}</ref>  His grandson is the [[Conductor (music)|conductor]] and [[composer]] [[Bertie Baigent]].

== Selected works ==
* Spectrum of Atomic Hydrogen, 1957
* Laser Spectroscopy and other topics, 1985
* Spectrum of Atomic Hydrogen: advances, 1988
